name: Little Black Mountain
generated_description:
At 3,488 feet, Little Black Mountain is a summit in Kentucky. The Little Black Mountain Trail covers 1.0 miles with about 253 feet of elevation gain — a gradual walk with modest climbing.

The Route

The climbing is spread fairly evenly from start to finish rather than stacked into one steep section. The steepest stretch arrives around mile 0.81, gaining roughly 900 feet per mile — expect a slow, deliberate pace through here. From the trailhead at about 1,591 feet, the route tops out near 1,831 feet.

Getting There

The trailhead is at 36.81165, -83.06226 (tap for driving directions). It's roughly 75 miles northeast of Knoxville, Tennessee. Arrive early on weekends — trailhead lots at popular peaks fill quickly, and cell service is often unreliable once you leave the highway.

When to Go

This trail is hikeable most of the year. Summer brings heat and humidity — carry extra water — while fall and spring offer the most comfortable conditions. Ice is possible on shaded stretches in mid-winter.

Know Before You Go

The Easy rating comes from the National Park Service difficulty formula, which weighs total distance against elevation gain. Most hikers should budget about 0.5 hours of moving time; add margin for breaks, photos and the descent. Download the GPX track from this page before you go — cell coverage is unreliable in the mountains and a saved route works offline in any GPS app. Conditions change: verify current access, closures and weather with the official land manager before you go. Trail data is sourced from OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).

Looking to link objectives or plan a weekend? Nearby summits include Joe Knob, Kitts Knob and Sugarcamp Knob — each has its own guide on this site.
